source_refs.note: Unnumbered heading Using Quantifiers in Logical Statements under 2.9, as printed (PDF 32, printed 28).

blocks.text: Quantifiers can be combined with predicates to make clear logical statements. For example, “∀x, P(x)” means the predicate P(x) is true for all x, while “∃x, P(x)” means P(x) is true for at least one x. Quantifiers can also be used together in complex statements. For instance, “∀x ∃y, x < y” means for every x there exists a y that is greater than x. Using quantifiers allows us to express rules, conditions, and relationships clearly.
